title: Usage event intake ambassador and progressive schema harmonization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a resilient, low-latency intake layer ("intake ambassador") for usage events destined for the Console analytics pipeline. The ambassador runs in front of existing collectors and performs lightweight validation, enrichment, and routing to the canonical event bus. This ticket covers design + implementation of the ambassador, a progressive schema harmonization strategy to support legacy and staged clients, and telemetry needed to measure acceptance and regression risks.
acceptance_criteria: Ambassador service deployed behind Console backend ingress that can accept production traffic at 7000 rps in a single AZ without errors.
Events failing validation are tagged with error codes and routed to dead-letter queue (DLQ) with schema mismatch metadata.
Progressive harmonization rules applied: auto-coerce simple type changes, namespace unknown fields under _unknown, and surface strict failures only after opt-in rollout.
End-to-end tests covering three canonical event shapes (generation, embedding, usage) run in CI and gating pipeline.
Dashboard showing per-client validation rates, top schema diffs, and DLQ growth is available in Grafana (console-usage-validate dashboard).
Performance budget: p95 latency for validation < 12ms for 1-token events, CPU overhead < 15% on reference instance compared to baseline collector.
tasks: Design: schema harmonization strategy + opt-in rollout plan (doc: Confluence/Console/Intake-Ambassador)
Proto: lightweight validation library (golang) with fast-path for common events and pluggable coercers
Implement ambassador service with async DLQ and backpressure-aware routing
Add metrics: validation_ok, validation_warn, validation_fail, dlq_enqueue_rate, per_client_rate
Integration tests for compatibility with existing event canonicalizer and telemetry ingest filter
Create Grafana dashboard and alerting rules for validation_fail spikes > 0.5% for 10m
Run gradual rollout: beta clients (10 customers) -> 50% traffic -> 100% after 2 weeks stability
discussion: 2025-11-04: Initial design review: preferred fast-path inlined JSON checks vs full JSON schema. Decision: implement composition of handwritten checks for hot paths and fallback to JSON schema validator for cold/complex events.
2025-11-06: Trade-off: stricter validation increases DLQ noise but prevents downstream regressions. Chosen approach: default permissive with opt-in strict mode per client.
2025-11-10: Security flagged that enrichment must not call external services synchronously; enrichment will be limited to header/meta transforms and async job for heavy enrichment.
2025-11-13: PM review (Lina Gomez): request to expose per-route cost tags for downstream billing; added to metrics tasks.
2025-11-15: Performance spike reproduced in staging when buffer size configured too low. Marcus adjusted batching defaults; follow-up to test different kernel sizes remains.
2025-11-17: UX asked for clear DLQ remediation guide; added Confluence section and example curl commands to reprocess DLQ items.
Notes: links to artifacts and PRs included below.
notes: We intentionally avoid heavyweight schema registry calls on the hot path. Instead the ambassador maintains a local compact schema cache refreshed via SSE. The cache format is compacted to keep memory usage bounded. We will monitor cache-miss rates and evict LRU entries if needed.
